title: Hardik Pandya Set for Punjab Kings Move in Arshdeep Swap, Reports Say
excerpt: Sportstar reports, via Sportskeeda and CricTracker, that Mumbai and Punjab have all but agreed a Pandya-for-Arshdeep and Vishnu Vinod exchange — unconfirmed by either franchise or the IPL.
body:
• According to reports, Mumbai Indians captain Hardik Pandya is set for a move to Punjab Kings, with Arshdeep Singh and Vishnu Vinod moving the other way — no franchise or the IPL has confirmed the trade.
  • Sportstar, as reported by Sportskeeda and CricTracker, says senior management at both franchises has all but agreed the exchange, with paperwork expected to go to IPL officials and a possible announcement before the November 17 retention deadline.
  • For diaspora IPL fans, nothing changes until an official announcement: treat this as a reported deal in progress, not a completed transfer.

Hardik Pandya is set for a move from Mumbai Indians to Punjab Kings in a swap involving Arshdeep Singh, according to reports — and that attribution matters, because neither franchise nor the IPL has confirmed any trade. Sportskeeda, citing a Sportstar report on November 3, says Punjab Kings are closing in on a trade for the Mumbai all-rounder ahead of IPL 2027, with India left-arm pacer Arshdeep Singh and wicketkeeper-batter Vishnu Vinod likely to move in the opposite direction.

What the reports say has been agreed

Senior management at both franchises has “all but agreed on the proposed exchange”, the Sportstar report says, with the paperwork expected to be processed by IPL officials. An announcement could follow later this week, before the November 17 retention deadline, Sportskeeda reports. CricTracker, also citing Sportstar, says the BCCI extended that retention cut-off from the original November 15 date after informing franchises on Monday of the revised timeline.

https://x.com/Sportskeeda/status/2117496183572820327

The report states that the first approach came from a senior Mumbai official. Punjab, coached by Ricky Ponting and captained by Shreyas Iyer, agreed to explore a deal, and talks settled on Arshdeep and Vinod as the return package, according to Sportskeeda. Mumbai sounded out several franchises; only Kolkata Knight Riders reached a comparable stage, discussing a multi-player package that did not progress as far. Neither report says whether Pandya would take the captaincy from Iyer, and Sportskeeda notes that neither franchise has addressed that question.

Why Arshdeep's reported exit is notable

Punjab's willingness to part with Arshdeep is the surprise inside the reported deal. The franchise released him before the IPL 2025 mega auction, then used its Right to Match card to bring him back after Sunrisers Hyderabad bid for him, Sportskeeda reports. He took 14 wickets in 13 matches in IPL 2026 at an economy of 10.21, and on April 16 at the Wankhede he became the first Punjab bowler to 100 IPL wickets, taking 3 for 22 against Mumbai.

His reported exit would leave a hole in Punjab's new-ball attack and could trigger a second trade, Sportskeeda reports: the franchise may approach Lucknow Super Giants about a swap involving left-arm pacer Mohsin Khan and Australian all-rounder Marcus Stoinis. CricTracker likewise reports that a Stoinis and Mohsin arrangement remains at a very early stage and unconfirmed.

The season behind the reports

The trade reports follow a poor season for Pandya by his own standards. Sportskeeda reports the Mumbai captain scored 206 runs in 10 matches in IPL 2026 at an average of 22.89 and a strike rate of 138.26, with a highest score of 40, and took four wickets. Mumbai finished ninth, with four wins from 14 matches. Pandya returned to Mumbai in an all-cash trade from Gujarat Titans before IPL 2024, after leading Gujarat to the title in 2022, and Mumbai retained him for Rs 16.35 crore before IPL 2026, according to Sportskeeda.

What happens next

Until Mumbai, Punjab or the IPL announces the trade, Pandya remains a Mumbai Indians player and Arshdeep and Vinod remain Punjab Kings players. The next fixed point in the reports is the November 17 retention deadline, by which franchises must confirm the players they are keeping ahead of IPL 2027. If the paperwork the reports describe is processed, an announcement later this week would make this one of the biggest trades of the window; if it is not, the reports will join the long list of trade-window deals that stayed on paper.
